evals.prompt:
Add Auth0 authentication to an Express Node.js application using the express-oauth2-jwt-bearer SDK.

**Auth0 Credentials:**
- Domain: `dev-example.auth0.com`
- Client ID: `abc123def456ghi789jkl012`
- API Audience: `https://api.example.com`
evals.expected_output: Working Express Node.js API with Auth0 JWT validation, protected endpoints, and RBAC permissions
expectations: Configures JWT Bearer token validation middleware
Configures API audience for token validation
Has protected API endpoint with JWT middleware
Auth0 domain dev-example.auth0.com written to .env config file
API audience https://api.example.com written to .env config file
No login UI methods or callback URLs in stateless API
No client secret in API config (uses JWKS for validation)
Solution correctly configures Auth0 JWT Bearer token validation, RBAC permissions, and CORS in an Express Node.js API
Pins the Auth0 SDK to an explicit version in the dependency declaration
Configures specific token validation options (clockTolerance or tokenSigningAlg)
Uses claim validation functions (requiredScopes, claimIncludes, claimCheck) for RBAC
Does not use deprecated express-jwt + jwks-rsa combo (uses current express-oauth2-jwt-bearer)
At least 2 skill-specific advanced patterns present (version, advanced validation options, RBAC, DPoP, CORS ordering)

graders.description: Auth0 issuer env var configured (AUTH0_DOMAIN per skill, or ISSUER_BASE_URL)
Configures JWT Bearer token validation middleware
Configures API audience for token validation
Has protected API endpoint with JWT middleware
Auth0 domain written to .env config file
API audience written to .env config file
No login UI methods or callback URLs in stateless API
No client secret in API config (uses JWKS for validation)

graders.question: Does the solution correctly configure Auth0 JWT Bearer token validation, RBAC permissions, and CORS in an Express Node.js API?
graders.examples:
PASS: Validates JWT using JWKS endpoint via express-oauth2-jwt-bearer, checks audience, applies checkJwt middleware to protected routes, configures CORS before auth.
FAIL: Uses client secret for token validation instead of JWKS.
FAIL: Has login routes or session cookies — APIs should be stateless JWT only.
FAIL: Uses @auth0/auth0-react or @auth0/auth0-spa-js — those are SPA SDKs, not API middleware.
graders.description: correctness-judge: Solution correctly integrates Auth0 JWT validation in Express API
Configures specific token validation options (clockTolerance or tokenSigningAlg)
Uses claim validation functions (requiredScopes, claimIncludes, claimCheck) for RBAC
Does not use deprecated express-jwt + jwks-rsa combo (uses current express-oauth2-jwt-bearer)

graders.question: Check ONLY for these skill-specific advanced patterns (NOT basic SDK usage like auth, checkJwt, app.use(auth, Authorization, Bearer). Look for at least 2 of: (1) an explicit pinned express-oauth2-jwt-bearer version in a dependency declaration (e.g. a caret/tilde/exact semver like '^1.7.4' in package.json — any explicit version, not 'latest' or absent), (2) specific validation options like clockTolerance or issuerBaseURL passed to auth() config object, (3) RBAC implementation using requiredScopes() or claimIncludes() with permissions claim, (4) DPoP configuration via dpop option, (5) CORS configured explicitly before auth middleware. These are advanced patterns taught by the skill that are NOT part of standard quickstart knowledge. Answer YES only if at least 2 of these advanced patterns are present, NO otherwise.
graders.examples:
PASS: Pins an explicit express-oauth2-jwt-bearer version in package.json AND uses requiredScopes() or claimIncludes() for RBAC authorization.
PASS: Sets clockTolerance in auth() config AND configures CORS middleware before auth middleware.
FAIL: Only configures basic auth() with issuerBaseURL and audience — no advanced options, no RBAC, no pinned version.
FAIL: Uses checkJwt correctly but has no permission checking beyond basic JWT validation and no advanced configuration.
graders.description: skill-attribution-judge: At least 2 skill-specific advanced patterns present (version, advanced validation options, RBAC, DPoP, CORS ordering)
